title: Sask. Indigenous leaders call for release of full report on P.A. police review
subtitle: The FSIN says the in-custody death of 33-year-old Saul Laliberte was avoidable. Laliberte's family was present at a media conference on Wednesday.
article: Saul Laliberte's mother and brother listened quietly Wednesday morning as Indigenous leaders called for the release of a full report produced by a review of the Prince Albert city police.
The province ordered the review after a series of deaths.

Laliberte was one of three people who died in Prince Albert police custody in 2021, prompting the Prince Albert Grand Council and Federation of Sovereign Indigenous Nations to call on the provincial government to intervene.

The province in November 2022 commissioned a review of the Prince Albert force's operations. On Tuesday, the government released the 45 recommendations in the final report of the review conducted by former Edmonton police chief Rod Knecht.
The report itself has not been released.

At a media conference hosted by the FSIN in Saskatoon, Vice-Chief Dutch Lerat said he wouldn't comment on the recommendations without the context of the review report being available. The full report should be released, he said.
The Ministry of Corrections, Policing and Public Safety said there are currently "no plans to publicly release the full report."

An emailed statement from the ministry added: "Transparency and accountability are critical to the work police do to keep Saskatchewan communities safe. At the same time, this work is inherently sensitive and often requires a certain degree of discretion and confidentiality.

"Maintaining public confidence and trust in policing is integral as the Prince Albert Police Service moves forward with implementing the recommendations and works to ensure an effective level of policing in the community."

Laliberte died after he was taken to the Prince Albert police detention centre on Nov. 7, 2021 . Last week, the force announced that a 21-year veteran officer had been charged with criminal negligence causing death and failure to provide the necessities of life.

The Crown recommended charges after the Saskatoon Police Service completed its investigation into Laliberte's death. The officer, Tyson Morash, 50, was removed from active duty pending the outcome of court proceedings.

Lerat said Laliberte's mother, Amelia Bloomfield, contacted Prince Albert police after her son's arrest out of concern for his well-being. She asked police to take her son to the hospital, believing him to be "at risk," he said.
"Her request was ignored and hours later, Saul was found dead in his cell."
Bloomfield is a knowledge keeper and Elder.
"The police service, at the time, never ensured his safety, and this was a tragedy that could have been avoided," Lerat said.

Laliberte had been taken into custody on outstanding warrants shortly before 3 p.m. to await a court appearance. He was found unresponsive in his cell at 7:30 p.m., a previous police release said . He was later pronounced dead at Victoria Hospital.
Lerat called on all police agencies to stop lodging people in custody for alcohol or drug intoxication, saying those cases are the responsibility of health authorities.
As of Wednesday, the family had not received a copy of the official autopsy report, which would indicate the cause of death.
Prince Albert Grand Council Grand Chief Brian Hardlotte called for immediate implementation of the review's recommendations and inclusion of the PAGC on the Prince Albert police board.

"(The) PAGC firmly believes that their inclusion will contribute valuable perspective, insight and expertise to the decision-making process," Hardlotte said, adding that he didn't see mention of inclusion of Elders or culturally relevant training in the recommendations.

Before the the review was commissioned, the PAGC and FSIN called for an investigation and firings after a 13-month old boy, Tanner Brass - who was in a home police attended to respond to a domestic violence call - was later found dead in February 2022. The toddler's father was charged with second-degree murder in his death.

A subsequent Public Complaints Commission investigation found the two responding officers took the boy's mother to the police station without checking on her son. It recommended the officers face "appropriate discipline" for "neglect of duty."
Cumberland House Chief Rene Chaboyer described Laliberte as a son, brother, friend and a person who should have been treated fairly like anyone.
"It's a shame that something like this event takes away a mother's baby, because of the system that we live in," Chaboyer said.
In Laliberte's memory, he wants to support the family as much as he can and air his disbelief that people within the system are treated similarly, he said.
"In memory of Saul, we must do better."
